chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Hilal, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about the son of a paternal brother and the son of a maternal brother. He said, 'For the son of the maternal brother is one-sixth, and whatever remains is for the son of the paternal brother.' I asked, 'Is this for the distribution (of the estate) or not?' He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'As far as I have been informed, the mother of the deceased has entered into this matter, meaning the debt.' He remained silent for a moment, then said, 'Take it.'

key_terms.ابْنِ الْأَخِ مِنَ الْأَبِ: son of a paternal brother (paternal cousin)
key_terms.ابْنِ الْأَخِ مِنَ الْأُمِّ: son of a maternal brother (maternal cousin)

ai.seo_question: What is the inheritance share of a maternal cousin versus a paternal cousin in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq clarifies the specific shares of paternal and maternal cousins (Ibn al-Akh) in the absence of closer heirs, establishing the maternal cousin's fixed one-sixth share and the paternal cousin's residual portion. The Imam’s brief pause before confirming the deduction of debts highlights the scholarly nuance in prioritizing the settlement of the deceased's liabilities before distributing the remainder to these collateral heirs. This ruling is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for understanding the hierarchy of 'Asabah and fixed-share heirs when the primary line of descent is absent.
